claim: People who do not vote for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in the 2020 elections will not get the COVID vaccine free of cost.
justification: The high-confidence evidence (scores 0.90 and 0.95) consistently shows that India's official COVID-19 vaccine policy, launched in January 2021, distributed free vaccines based on public health criteria like age and occupation, with no documented condition tied to voting for the BJP. While some low-confidence evidence (score 0.10) suggests BJP officials made rhetorical statements during the 2020 Bihar elections, these were political promises for state governance contingent on winning, not implemented policies of discrimination. The claim describes an enforced policy of exclusion, which is refuted by the trusted evidence on the actual vaccination program's structure and administration.
